html:
An Ivorian novelist from a Malinke family of the north, whose first book, The Suns of Independence (Les Soleils des independances, 1968), mocked the hopes and failures of the new African states.

He wrote French bent to the rhythms and proverbs of Malinke, a new voice in African literature in French. Jailed briefly under Houphouet-Boigny, he spent years in exile. Waiting for the Wild Beasts to Vote (1998) satirised Cold War dictators, and Allah Is Not Obliged (2000), told by a child soldier in the wars of Liberia and Sierra Leone, won the Prix Renaudot. He died in France while writing about the Ivorian civil war.
